outages.place: Paraná, including the North, West, Northwest, and other regions
outages.cause: Storms and two F1 tornadoes that damaged the electrical system with strong wind gusts, lightning, and fallen trees, according to Copel, with Simepar confirming the tornadoes
outages.affected: Copel, as reported by TNOnline in an article published at 2:34 p.m. Brasília time Monday, Nov 23 (11:34 a.m. CT), and by Paiquerê FM News at 1:44 p.m. Brasília time Monday (10:44 a.m. CT), said that 98.7 percent of service had already been restored and that approximately 4,600 consumer units remained without power across Paraná as of Monday morning, Nov 23. Those reports, citing Copel, said the remaining outages were concentrated in the West (1,528 units), the North (1,010), the Southwest (772), the East, covering Curitiba, the metropolitan region, and the coast (676), the Northwest (541), and Centro-Sul (85). TNOnline, citing the latest state Civil Defense bulletin, also said the damage began on Friday, Nov 20, with two tornadoes in Foz do Iguaçu and Manoel Ribas and with windstorms and hail that affected 10 other cities over the weekend, and that the storms had caused 353,800 simultaneous disconnections at the most critical moment of the event. The same report, citing the state, said a joint Copel and Sanepar operation using large generators and water-tank trucks had been used to protect essential water service in cities including Foz do Iguaçu, Cascavel, Maringá, Apucarana, and Londrina after outages temporarily affected water intake, treatment, and distribution in the West, Northwest, and North, and that the water system had already been fully normalized. Almanaque Futuro, in an article dated Nov 23, 2026, citing the Copel operations panel consulted at 10:47 a.m. Brasília time Monday (7:47 a.m. CT), said 979 consumer units remained without power in Foz do Iguaçu, about 1 percent of the municipality's customers, down from a Friday peak of about 36,000 units in that city, and that some interruptions there had already lasted more than 68 hours; the same report said the Morumbi neighborhood accounted for the largest share, with 414 units out. No official firm restoration time for all remaining customers in Paraná was given. An earlier Copel bulletin issued at 7:00 p.m. Brasília time Sunday, Nov 22 (4:00 p.m. CT), as reported by Umuarama News on Sunday and by TNOnline at 7:26 p.m. Brasília time Sunday (4:26 p.m. CT), had said that 98 percent of the affected consumer units had already been restored and that approximately 8,800 units remained without power at that earlier hour, concentrated in the West (2,700), the North (2,200), the Northwest (1,500), the Southwest (1,100), the East (767), and Centro-Sul (401). An earlier Sunday 12:30 p.m. Brasília time Copel bulletin, as reported by Umuarama News, OBemdito, CBN Curitiba, Tribuna do Interior, and Maringá Atual, had said approximately 16,700 units remained without power and that more than 96.5 percent had already been reconnected. An earlier Copel bulletin as of 6:30 p.m. Brasília time Saturday, Nov 21 (3:30 p.m. CT), as reported by CGN and Folha de Curitiba, had said 54,246 units remained without power and that 299,603 units, or 85 percent, had already been reconnected. An earlier noon Saturday Copel bulletin, as reported by Tribuna do Interior, said 80,588 units remained without power at that earlier hour, 273,261 had been restored (77.2 percent), and the peak had been 353,849 units at 8:02 p.m. Brasília time Friday, Nov 20 (5:02 p.m. CT Friday). Simepar confirmed two F1 tornadoes on Friday, Nov 20, one around 3:00 p.m. Brasília time (noon CT Friday) in the Vila Yolanda neighborhood of Foz do Iguaçu and another around 6:00 p.m. Brasília time (3:00 p.m. CT Friday) in Manoel Ribas, with estimated winds of 117 to 180 km/h. No later official Copel remaining-customer count after the Monday morning figure of approximately 4,600 was found as of 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (3:00 p.m. Brasília time Monday).
outages.start: Afternoon and evening of Friday, Nov 20, 2026 (Brasília time), when storms and two F1 tornadoes hit Paraná; the peak of 353,849 consumer units was recorded at 8:02 p.m. Brasília time Friday (5:02 p.m. CT Friday), according to Copel's Saturday noon bulletin as reported by Tribuna do Interior
outages.updated: Nov 23, 2026, Copel Monday morning remaining count of approximately 4,600 consumer units and 98.7 percent already restored, via TNOnline published 2:34 p.m. Brasília time Monday, Nov 23 (= 11:34 a.m. CT) and Paiquerê FM News at 1:44 p.m. Brasília time Monday (= 10:44 a.m. CT), with remaining outages concentrated in the West (1,528), North (1,010), Southwest (772), East (676), Northwest (541), and Centro-Sul (85); Almanaque Futuro, citing the Copel operations panel consulted at 10:47 a.m. Brasília time Monday (= 7:47 a.m. CT), on 979 consumer units still without power in Foz do Iguaçu; earlier Sunday 7:00 p.m. Brasília time Copel bulletin of approximately 8,800 still out and 98 percent restored, via Umuarama News and TNOnline; earlier Sunday 12:30 p.m. Brasília time bulletin of approximately 16,700 still out; earlier Saturday 6:30 p.m. Brasília time figure of 54,246 still out; earlier noon Saturday bulletin via Tribuna do Interior on 80,588 still out and a Friday peak of 353,849 units at 8:02 p.m. Brasília time Friday; Simepar confirmation of two Friday F1 tornadoes in Foz do Iguaçu and Manoel Ribas; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (3:00 p.m. Brasília time Monday), no later official Copel remaining-customer count found

outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale attack on Nov 20 and further strikes reported on Nov 21 and into Nov 22 and Nov 23. Ukrenergo said planned outage schedules would be in effect around the clock on Monday, Nov 23, in parts of the country because of those attacks
outages.affected: Kyiv Post, in an article dated 2:18 p.m. Monday, Nov 23 (7:18 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), citing Ukraine's Energy Ministry and First Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov, said Russia had carried out 100 attacks on Ukraine's energy, oil, and gas infrastructure over the past week, contributing to 224 recorded damage incidents, and that power outages had continued to affect seven regions on Monday, Nov 23: Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zhytomyr, Sumy, Kharkiv, Odesa, and Poltava, with the situation remaining particularly difficult in Odesa and Dnipropetrovsk regions. The same report, citing Nekrasov, said energy workers had restored power to critical infrastructure facilities while repairs and efforts to reconnect households and businesses continued; that grid restrictions had been introduced in Dnipropetrovsk region to prevent further outages caused by overloads; that emergency power cuts remained in place in Kharkiv region because of previous damage and reduced voltage in the high-voltage transmission network, with scheduled outages to resume once the situation stabilized; and that Russian forces had also struck a gas-infrastructure facility in Dnipropetrovsk region in the previous days, injuring three employees. Kyiv Post also said that across most of Ukraine, hourly electricity outage schedules were in place on Nov 23, while industrial consumers faced power restrictions, and, citing Ukraine's Air Force data reported by Ukrainian media, that on the night of Nov 23 Russia launched 153 attack drones against Ukraine, including 60 jet-powered Shahed drones, alongside Gerbera drones and Parodiya decoys. Earlier Monday morning reports had given a similar ministry account: Ukrenergo, as reported by UNN at 10:11 a.m. Kyiv time Monday, Nov 23 (2:11 a.m. CT) and by Slovo i Dilo at 12:38 p.m. EET Monday (4:38 a.m. CT), said that restoration work continued throughout the night in Odesa and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts, that the situation in Odesa Oblast had been partially stabilized and electricity supply to critical infrastructure in Odesa had been restored, and that the situation in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast remained significantly more difficult, with hourly outage schedules in effect in the region. Those Monday morning reports, citing Ukrenergo, also said that on Monday, Nov 23, planned restrictions would be in effect around the clock in some regions: capacity-limitation schedules for industry, and hourly outage schedules of 1 to 4 queues for all categories of consumers. Vidomo, in an article dated 10:59 a.m. Monday, Nov 23 (2:59 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), citing the Energy Ministry and Nekrasov, said that as of the morning of Nov 23 some consumers remained without power in the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zhytomyr, Odesa, Poltava, Sumy, and Kharkiv regions because of shelling and combat, and that in Kharkiv region emergency outages had been applied because of a voltage drop in the high-voltage network. An earlier Sunday night Ukrenergo statement, as reported by Censor.NET at 10:24 p.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22 (2:24 p.m. CT), by UNIAN at 11:13 p.m. EET Sunday (3:13 p.m. CT), by Focus, and by 24tv, had said that on Monday, Nov 23, planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock in parts of the country: hourly outage schedules of 1 to 3.5 groups, or queues, for all categories of consumers, and capacity-restriction schedules for industry. UNIAN, in that Sunday night report, said those 1 to 3.5 queues amounted to approximately 4 to 16 hours a day for household consumers. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, in his Sunday evening address as reported by Ukrinform at 9:09 p.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22 (1:09 p.m. CT) and by 24tv, said Russian forces were now using a tactic of destroying networks and transmission lines in an effort to cut Odesa, Odesa region, and Dnipropetrovsk region off from energy sources, and that the situation there was very difficult. No official nationwide customer count was found as of 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (8:00 p.m. EET Monday).

outages.place: Odesa and parts of Odesa district
outages.cause: Repeated Russian attacks on high-voltage transmission networks and other energy facilities critical to the region, including a strike on a DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi energy facility on the morning of Nov 20. Ukrenergo said on Monday, Nov 23, that the situation in Odesa Oblast had been partially stabilized and that electricity supply to critical infrastructure in Odesa had been restored, after main power grids suffered serious damage; Odesa regional governor Oleh Kiper said emergency outages without schedules were still being applied because the damaged equipment could not yet supply all consumers at once
outages.affected: Odesa regional governor Oleh Kiper, as reported by Censor.NET at 12:35 p.m. EET Monday, Nov 23 (4:35 a.m. CT), by UNN at 10:11 a.m. Kyiv time Monday (2:11 a.m. CT), and by Slovo i Dilo at 12:38 p.m. EET Monday (4:38 a.m. CT), said the electricity-supply situation in Odesa region remained difficult but that measures were being taken to stabilize it; that as a result of Russian attacks, Ukrenergo's main transmission network supplying Odesa and surrounding communities had sustained significant damage, and that given the scale of the destruction, restoration would take time; that all critical-infrastructure facilities and some consumers had already been energized; and that emergency outages without schedules were still being applied in Odesa District, including Odesa, because the damaged equipment did not yet allow electricity to be supplied to all consumers at the same time. Kiper, in those reports, said there was water in all districts of the city, though some apartment buildings might experience interruptions in water pumping; that of 11 large boiler houses, 9 were already operating, while 2 boiler houses and the combined heat and power plant were being brought online; that 130 small boiler houses were operating and 18 more would be launched shortly; and that heat had already been supplied to 186,000 subscribers, while about 79,000 consumers were temporarily without heating. Ukrenergo, as reported by UNN and Slovo i Dilo on Monday, said the situation in Odesa Oblast had been partially stabilized and that electricity supply to critical infrastructure in Odesa had been restored, after restoration work continued throughout the night. UNN also reported that Odesa City Military Administration head Serhii Lysak said in the morning that the past two days had been a test for Odesa and that, because of the enemy strike on the region's energy infrastructure, the city had been left without electricity, heating, or water; that deputy head Serhii Krasilenko said water supply had already been restored in all districts of Odesa thanks to backup power; and that, according to the Odesa City Council, as of the morning of Nov 23 the city's electric transport had been temporarily suspended, while schools and kindergartens where heating was restored would operate as usual on Tuesday, Nov 24. No official remaining-electricity-customer count was given in those Monday reports. Earlier Friday DTEK figures, cited in prior official and local reporting, had put remaining households at 8,000 families after the morning attack, after an earlier Friday morning figure of 41,000 households. No official remaining-electricity-customer count after those earlier Friday DTEK figures was found as of 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (8:00 p.m. EET Monday).
outages.updated: Nov 23, 2026, Odesa regional governor Oleh Kiper via Censor.NET 12:35 p.m. EET Monday, Nov 23 (= 4:35 a.m. CT), UNN 10:11 a.m. Kyiv time Monday (= 2:11 a.m. CT), and Slovo i Dilo 12:38 p.m. EET Monday (= 4:38 a.m. CT), on a still-difficult supply situation, emergency outages without schedules still being applied in Odesa District including Odesa, all critical infrastructure and some consumers already energized, water in all districts with possible pumping interruptions in some apartment buildings, 9 of 11 large boiler houses operating and 2 plus the CHP being brought online, heat already supplied to 186,000 subscribers, and about 79,000 consumers temporarily without heating; Ukrenergo Monday statement via UNN and Slovo i Dilo that the Odesa Oblast situation had been partially stabilized and that critical infrastructure in Odesa had been restored after overnight repair work; Odesa City Military Administration head Serhii Lysak and deputy head Serhii Krasilenko, and the Odesa City Council, via UNN, on the city having been left without electricity, heating, or water, on water supply restored in all districts with backup power, on electric transport temporarily suspended as of Monday morning, and on schools and kindergartens with restored heating to operate as usual on Tuesday, Nov 24; earlier Friday DTEK remaining 8,000 families after the morning attack and earlier Friday morning 41,000-household figure; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (8:00 p.m. EET Monday), no official remaining-electricity-customer count after the earlier Friday DTEK figures found

outages.place: Dnipro and parts of Dnipropetrovsk region, including Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, Kamianske, and Pavlohrad districts
outages.cause: Russian attacks that significantly damaged energy infrastructure in the region, according to Ukrenergo and Ukraine's Energy Ministry. First Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov said network restrictions were introduced to avoid accidents from overloaded equipment, and regional officials said emergency outages were in effect in Dnipro and several districts
outages.affected: Ukrenergo, as reported by UNN at 10:11 a.m. Kyiv time Monday, Nov 23 (2:11 a.m. CT) and by Slovo i Dilo at 12:38 p.m. EET Monday (4:38 a.m. CT), said the situation in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast remained significantly more difficult, that hourly outage schedules were in effect in the region, and that power engineers were continuing work to reduce the scope of the restrictions as quickly as possible, after restoration work continued throughout the night where energy infrastructure was significantly damaged as a result of Russian attacks. Vidomo, in an article dated 10:59 a.m. Monday, Nov 23 (2:59 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), citing Dnipropetrovsk regional council head Mykola Lukashuk, said that as of Nov 23 emergency outages remained in effect in Dnipro and in the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, Kamianske, and Pavlohrad districts, and that DTEK hourly outage schedules were not being applied in those communities. The same report said that for customers of the Central Energy Company (CEK), the region's other distribution-system operator, an hourly outage schedule was in effect on Nov 23, and that a separate schedule had been formed for part of the city of Pavlohrad. Vidomo, citing First Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov, said the situation in the energy system of Dnipropetrovsk and Odesa regions remained difficult because of large-scale destruction of energy facilities that supply those regions; that critical infrastructure had been energized; that network restrictions had been introduced in Dnipropetrovsk region to avoid accidents from overloaded equipment; and that electricity was being returned to consumers in stages. The Energy Ministry, as reported by Vidomo, also said that as of the morning of Nov 23 some consumers in Dnipropetrovsk region remained without power because of shelling and combat, and that a gas-infrastructure facility in the region had been attacked the previous day, injuring three workers. No official customer count was given in those reports as of 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (8:00 p.m. EET Monday).
outages.updated: Nov 23, 2026, Ukrenergo via UNN 10:11 a.m. Kyiv time Monday, Nov 23 (= 2:11 a.m. CT) and Slovo i Dilo 12:38 p.m. EET Monday (= 4:38 a.m. CT), saying the Dnipropetrovsk Oblast situation remained significantly more difficult, with hourly outage schedules in effect and overnight restoration work after significant damage from Russian attacks; Dnipropetrovsk regional council head Mykola Lukashuk via Vidomo 10:59 a.m. Monday (= 2:59 a.m. CT if Kyiv time / EET), on emergency outages remaining in effect in Dnipro and in the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, Kamianske, and Pavlohrad districts where DTEK hourly schedules were not being applied, with an hourly schedule in effect for Central Energy Company (CEK) customers and a separate schedule for part of Pavlohrad; First Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov and the Energy Ministry via Vidomo, on network restrictions to avoid accidents from overloaded equipment, critical infrastructure energized, power being returned in stages, some consumers still without power as of Monday morning because of shelling and combat, and a previous-day attack on a gas-infrastructure facility that injured three workers; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (8:00 p.m. EET Monday), no official customer count found

outages.place: Kurdistan Region, including Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal
outages.cause: Suspected drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field on the night of Nov 8, 2026, which halted gas production that supplies much of the region's electricity generation. Dana Gas, the field's operator, later said the facility had sustained significant damage and could produce no gas
outages.affected: Kurdistan24, in a Nov 22, 2026 report, said a trilateral meeting of the Kurdistan Regional Government, Iraq's Oil Ministry, and Dana Gas was expected within the next two days to discuss procedures for restarting natural gas production and delivery from the Khor Mor field. A KRG source told Kurdistan24 that a restart depends on Dana Gas obtaining security approval so it can resume operations, and that official results of investigations into the Nov 8 attack had not yet been made public. The same report said the Nov 8 drone attack in Sulaimani province caused a large fire and stopped gas production entirely, with no casualties, and that the stoppage cut 2,500 to 2,800 megawatts of electricity in the Kurdistan Region and reduced power-supply hours by five to six hours a day. That account is consistent with earlier official figures: Al Jazeera, on Nov 9, citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials and the official Iraqi News Agency, said the attack left more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region without power and, citing Omed Ahmed, spokesperson for the KRG Ministry of Electricity, that it suspended gas supply to power plants in Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Bazian, Chamchamal, and Duhok and knocked between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts off the grid. Rudaw later quoted Ahmed as saying authorities had increased generation from approximately 1,000 megawatts immediately after the attack to 1,550 megawatts, of which 50 megawatts were reserved for essential facilities and factories, leaving 1,500 megawatts for residents and raising daily public electricity supply to six to eight hours; Ahmed said the electricity then available covered only 40 percent of demand, leaving a 60 percent shortfall, and that no date had been established for production to resume. Rudaw's article image assets for that report are dated Nov 13, 2026. 964media, in a Nov 15 report, quoted Ahmed as saying that no timeframe had been set for supplies to return to normal and that within 48 hours of the attack generation had been increased from 1,000 megawatts to nearly 1,650 megawatts. Dana Gas, in a Nov 14 clarification later restated in coverage including a Kurdistan24 report, said the facility had sustained significant damage and that no gas could currently be produced. The Insight International, in a Nov 21 report citing private-generator officials who spoke to Rudaw on Saturday, Nov 21, said the public grid remained weak because of the gas shortfall and that neighborhood generators were still running for most of the day in Erbil, Sulaimani, and Duhok. The New Region, in a Nov 22, 2026 report, said delegations from the Kurdistan Regional Government's natural resources ministry and from Iraq's oil ministry were set to meet Dana Gas on Monday, Nov 23, to discuss resuming gas production and supplies to power plants; that Dana Gas was expected to insist on security guarantees against further attacks; and that if an agreement were reached on Monday, a specialized Turkish company would begin repairs estimated to take six days. No official customer count was given. No later official ministry generation figure, and no official confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed or that a Monday agreement on repairs had been reached, was found as of 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (9:00 p.m. Iraq time Monday).
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. The New Region, in a Nov 22, 2026 report, said delegations from Erbil and Baghdad were set to meet Dana Gas on Monday, Nov 23, to discuss resuming production, that Dana Gas was expected to insist on security guarantees against further attacks, and that if an agreement were reached on Monday, a specialized Turkish company would begin repairs estimated to take six days. A KRG source told Kurdistan24 on Nov 22 that a restart depends on Dana Gas obtaining security approval. As of the latest official statements found, Khor Mor production had not been confirmed as having resumed, and no firm date had been established for production to resume.
outages.updated: Nov 22–23, 2026, The New Region dated Nov 22, 2026, on a planned Monday, Nov 23, meeting of Erbil and Baghdad delegations with Dana Gas on restarting Khor Mor production, with Dana Gas expected to seek security guarantees and, if an agreement were reached Monday, a specialized Turkish company to begin repairs estimated at six days; earlier Kurdistan24 on a planned trilateral meeting within two days on restarting Khor Mor production, with a KRG source saying a restart depends on Dana Gas obtaining security approval, and on the field remaining shut after the Nov 8 attack that cut 2,500 to 2,800 megawatts and reduced supply hours by five to six hours a day; earlier Al Jazeera Nov 9 citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials and INA; KRG electricity ministry figures via Rudaw (article image assets dated Nov 13) and 964media Nov 15; Dana Gas still-shut statement of Nov 14; The Insight International Nov 21, citing private-generator officials who spoke to Rudaw on Saturday, Nov 21, on the public-grid shortfall continuing; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (9:00 p.m. Iraq time Monday), no later official generation figure or confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed or that a Monday repair agreement had been reached found

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Yenakiieve, Khartsyzk, Zuhres, Torez, Snizhne, and nearby districts
outages.cause: Attacks on energy infrastructure, including a massive attack on the night of Nov 22, 2026, according to occupation officials, who said attacks on energy facilities were repeated the following night and that new outages were added to the effects of earlier damage; occupation officials also described a power deficit and forced temporary outages to prevent accidents
outages.affected: Occupation government head Andrei Chertkov, as reported by DAN at 6:34 p.m. Monday, Nov 23 (9:34 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said that electricity had been restored to the majority of subscribers in the territory who had been without power over the previous two days after attacks, that a significant part of subscribers had already been reconnected, that work was continuing, and that they expected to return electricity to all remaining consumers by the end of Monday. Chertkov, as quoted by DAN, also said energy workers were having to repair new damage and return to sections where power had only recently been restored, and that a capacity deficit caused by damaged equipment was leading to temporary outages in some municipalities to avoid overloads and further accidents. That evening statement did not give a new remaining-customer count. The last official count found was from the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, as reported by RIA Novosti at 12:50 p.m. Monday, Nov 23 (3:50 a.m. CT if Moscow time) and by DNR News at 9:48 a.m. Monday (12:48 a.m. CT if Moscow time), which said that as of Monday morning slightly more than 207,000 subscribers remained without electricity after attacks on the energy system, and that restoration work was continuing despite the threat of further strikes. RIA Novosti, citing the ministry, said attacks on energy facilities had been repeated the previous night, that no specialists had been injured, and that partial outages had been recorded in Donetsk, Makiivka, the Amvrosiivka, Volnovakha, Telmanove, Shakhtarsk, and Yasynuvata municipal districts, and in Khartsyzk, Zuhres, Torez, Snizhne, and Yenakiieve. A morning report by Lenta novostei Donetska dated 9:32 a.m. Monday, Nov 23 (12:32 a.m. CT if Moscow time), also said 249 boiler houses had been stopped. The Makiivka occupation administration, as reported by Lenta novostei Makeevki at 7:16 p.m. Monday, Nov 23 (10:16 a.m. CT if Moscow time), citing the Makiivka city electric networks branch of the South-West Electric Grid Company, said that as of 6:20 p.m. Monday (9:20 a.m. CT if Moscow time) several districts remained without power because of emergency disconnections and increased load on the networks, including parts of the Chervonohvardeiske, Horniatske, Kirovskyi, and Tsentralno-Miskyi districts and part of the city center, and that heating might also be temporarily interrupted; that report did not give a customer count. Vedomosti, in a Nov 23, 2026 report, citing Donetsk occupation mayor Alexei Kulemzin and data from the Donetskenergo branch of the South-West Electric Grid Company, said 114,648 subscribers remained without electricity in Donetsk city, that partial outages had affected all districts of the city, and that 551 transformer substations were de-energized. An earlier Sunday statement by Chertkov, as reported by DNR News on Nov 22, had said more than 279,000 subscribers were without power after attacks, including partial outages in Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Yenakiieve, Debaltseve, Torez, and Snizhne and in settlements of several municipal districts. No later official remaining-customer count after the Monday morning figure of slightly more than 207,000 was found as of 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (9:00 p.m. Moscow time Monday).
outages.start: Night of Sunday, Nov 22, 2026, local time, for the attack described by occupation officials; occupation officials said attacks on energy facilities were repeated the following night; other partial outages in the region were already being reported
outages.etr: Occupation government head Andrei Chertkov, as reported by DAN at 6:34 p.m. Monday, Nov 23 (9:34 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said that a significant part of subscribers had already been reconnected and that they expected to return electricity to all remaining consumers by the end of Monday. An earlier Sunday statement by Chertkov, as reported by DNR News at 5:45 p.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (8:45 a.m. CT if Moscow time), had said restoration of the damaged energy center would take roughly two to three weeks. Donetsk occupation mayor Alexei Kulemzin, as reported by Vedomosti on Nov 23, did not give a time for full restoration of electricity in the city. No later official remaining-customer count was given with the Monday evening statement.
outages.updated: Nov 23, 2026, occupation government head Andrei Chertkov via DAN 6:34 p.m. Monday, Nov 23 (= 9:34 a.m. CT if Moscow time), saying electricity had been restored to the majority of subscribers left without power over the previous two days, that a significant part had already been reconnected, and that they expected to restore the remainder by the end of Monday, without giving a new remaining-customer count; earlier Monday morning occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy count of slightly more than 207,000 subscribers still out as of Monday morning, via RIA Novosti 12:50 p.m. Monday (= 3:50 a.m. CT if Moscow time) and DNR News 9:48 a.m. Monday (= 12:48 a.m. CT if Moscow time), with partial outages listed in Donetsk, Makiivka, and other cities and districts; Lenta novostei Donetska 9:32 a.m. Monday (= 12:32 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on 249 boiler houses stopped; Makiivka occupation administration via Lenta novostei Makeevki 7:16 p.m. Monday (= 10:16 a.m. CT if Moscow time), citing the local grid branch as of 6:20 p.m. Monday (= 9:20 a.m. CT), on remaining emergency outages in several districts, without a customer count; Vedomosti Nov 23 report citing Donetsk occupation mayor Alexei Kulemzin on 114,648 subscribers without electricity in Donetsk city and 551 de-energized transformer substations; earlier Sunday Chertkov figure of more than 279,000 subscribers via DNR News Nov 22, and his Sunday estimate of roughly two to three weeks to restore the damaged energy center; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (9:00 p.m. Moscow time Monday), no later official remaining-customer count found

outages.place: Crimea and Sevastopol, including Yevpatoria, Dzhankoy, Bilohirsk, Feodosia, Alushta, and other districts
outages.cause: A power-capacity shortage after strikes on transmission networks outside the peninsula, according to occupation sources. Krymenergo said a consumption-restriction regime was introduced on Monday morning, Nov 23, by command of the federal system operator, and later Monday notices described further rolling outages of about three hours in multiple districts
outages.affected: Krymenergo, as posted by Lenta novostei Kryma at 7:21 p.m. Monday, Nov 23 (10:21 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said that because of the introduced consumption limits, electricity supply was partially absent in Feodosia in the central part of the city; in the area of the traffic police, the hosiery factory, the winery, and Forshtadt; and on Admiralsky Boulevard and Desantnikov, Shmidta, Ukrainskaya, and Nazarova streets and adjacent streets and lanes, with an approximate outage duration of three hours. An earlier Krymenergo notice, as posted by Lenta novostei Kryma at 5:01 p.m. Monday, Nov 23 (8:01 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said that because of the introduced limits, electricity would be cut from approximately 7:00 p.m. Monday (10:00 a.m. CT) in Bakhchisaray district in Bakhchisaray (Michurina Street), Siren, Mostovoye, and Zheleznodorozhnoye, and partially in Rechnoye, for an approximate duration of three hours. Earlier Monday, Krymenergo, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 10:24 a.m. Monday, Nov 23 (1:24 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said electricity supply had been temporarily restricted in several cities and districts because of the introduced consumption limits, and that the approximate duration of the outages was three hours. That report, citing Krymenergo, listed outages or scheduled cuts in the Pervomaiske, Saky, Bilohirsk, Bakhchisaray, Dzhankoy city and district, Sovetskyi, Lenine, and Kirovske districts, partial outages in Chornomorske district, partial outages in the center of Feodosia and in the area of Poleva and Volodarskoho streets, and additional streets in Yevpatoria. Alushta administration head Galina Ogneva, as quoted in the same report, said a rolling-outage schedule was in effect throughout the municipality because of insufficient available capacity. Rossiyskaya Gazeta, in an article dated 10:03 a.m. Monday, Nov 23 (1:03 a.m. CT if Moscow time), also said eight rural districts were partially without power — Saky, Bilohirsk, Bakhchisaray, and Dzhankoy, and later Chornomorske, Lenine, Kirovske, and Sovetskyi — with an approximate restoration time of three hours, and that a limited-consumption regime continued in Crimea and Sevastopol; the same report said Sevastopol was operating on a two-through-six schedule, with two hours of electricity alternating with six hours without power. A later morning Krymenergo notice, as posted by Crimea-News at 2:21 p.m. Monday, Nov 23 (5:21 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said that from approximately 2:30 p.m. local time Monday (5:30 a.m. CT) electricity would be cut in Lenine district in Oktyabrske, Baherove, Ivanivka, Novoselivka, and Gornostaevka, and partially in Fontan and Pryozerne, for an approximate duration of three hours. An earlier Krymenergo update, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 8:18 a.m. Monday, updated at 8:37 a.m. Monday (11:18 p.m. and 11:37 p.m. CT Sunday, Nov 22, if Moscow time), had said a consumption-restriction regime was introduced Monday morning by command of the federal system operator, with outages expected to last about three to six hours, and had listed Monday morning outages in more than 20 localities in Dzhankoy district and in streets and garden associations in Yevpatoria. Occupation sources have said peninsula-wide interruptions began Oct 24, 2026, after strikes on transmission networks outside the peninsula. No official customer count was given in those Monday reports as of 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (9:00 p.m. Moscow time Monday).

outages.cause: Generation-capacity deficit in the national electric system. UNE's Monday bulletin said unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz and unit 2 of CTE Felton were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance, with thermal-generation limitations of 446 MW
outages.affected: UNE's Monday bulletin, published by Juventud Rebelde at 8:35 a.m. Cuba time Monday, Nov 23 (7:35 a.m. CT) and updated at 10:15 a.m. Cuba time Monday (9:15 a.m. CT), said service had been affected by a generation-capacity deficit throughout all 24 hours on Sunday, Nov 22, and that the affectation continued through the early morning. The published bulletin text said the maximum Sunday affectation by generation-capacity deficit was recorded at 6:50 p.m. Cuba time Sunday (5:50 p.m. CT Sunday), but it did not state the megawatt figure for that Sunday peak. No official Sunday evening-peak actual in megawatts was found. The bulletin said solar-photovoltaic parks produced 4,601 MWh on Sunday, with a maximum of 715 MW delivered in the midday period. At 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Monday (5:00 a.m. CT), it said, 1,105 MW was available, demand was 2,135 MW, and 1,039 MW was affected, and it estimated a midday affectation of 1,200 MW. For the evening peak, it estimated 1,105 MW available and a maximum demand of 2,800 MW, for a deficit of 1,695 MW, and, if those conditions held, a forecast affectation of 1,725 MW. It said unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz and unit 2 of CTE Felton were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance, with thermal-generation limitations of 446 MW. CiberCuba, in an article dated 11:35 a.m. Monday, Nov 23 (10:35 a.m. CT if Cuba time), said UNE had reported the emergency exit of unit 3 of CTE Antonio Maceo (Renté) at 9:01 a.m. Monday (8:01 a.m. CT if Cuba time), after the morning bulletin had already been issued; that additional outage was not listed in the morning UNE bulletin's breakdown or maintenance units. An earlier official UNE Sunday bulletin, published by Granma at 10:11 a.m. Cuba time Sunday, Nov 22 (9:11 a.m. CT), had said the Saturday, Nov 21, maximum affectation was 1,778 MW at 6:50 p.m. Cuba time Saturday (5:50 p.m. CT Saturday), and had forecast a Sunday evening-peak affectation of 1,713 MW against a forecast 1,117 MW available and 2,800 MW demand. No official Monday evening-peak actual from UNE was found as of 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (1:00 p.m. Cuba time Monday).
outages.updated: Nov 23, 2026, official UNE Monday bulletin via Juventud Rebelde published 8:35 a.m. Cuba time Monday, Nov 23 (= 7:35 a.m. CT) and updated 10:15 a.m. Cuba time Monday (= 9:15 a.m. CT), including Sunday service affected by a generation-capacity deficit throughout all 24 hours, Monday 6:00 a.m. Cuba time figures of 1,105 MW available, 2,135 MW demand, and 1,039 MW affected, a midday estimate of 1,200 MW, and a Monday evening-peak forecast affectation of 1,725 MW against a forecast 1,105 MW available and 2,800 MW demand; the published Monday bulletin text did not state the megawatt figure for Sunday's 6:50 p.m. peak; CiberCuba dated 11:35 a.m. Monday (= 10:35 a.m. CT if Cuba time) on the emergency exit of Renté unit 3 at 9:01 a.m. Monday; earlier official UNE Sunday bulletin via Granma 10:11 a.m. Cuba time Sunday (= 9:11 a.m. CT) on Saturday's maximum affectation of 1,778 MW at 6:50 p.m. Cuba time Saturday and a Sunday peak forecast of 1,713 MW; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (1:00 p.m. Cuba time Monday), no official Sunday evening-peak actual in megawatts and no official Monday evening-peak actual found

outages.cause: Planned electricity restrictions that Tavanir said began Sunday, Nov 22, 2026, because fuel shortages were disrupting power generation
outages.affected: The National, in an article dated November 23, 2026, and marked updated at 5:00 AM, said Iran had begun imposing scheduled power cuts on consumers because of difficulties supplying fuel to power plants, according to state electricity company Tavanir. The article quoted Tavanir chief executive Mohammad Allahdad telling state television on Sunday that the restrictions were initially expected to last up to two hours every other day, rising to two hours daily if temperatures dropped further, and that, given the country's fuel-supply conditions, the electricity sector would be forced to impose distribution restrictions from Sunday. The National also quoted Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, as reported by the Isna news agency, saying the attack on the country's gas infrastructure had aggravated the situation and that difficulties should therefore be expected this winter. Iran International, in a report dated 1:17 p.m. GMT Sunday, Nov 22 (7:17 a.m. CT), said scheduled power cuts had resumed across Iran, disrupting homes, businesses, and schools. It said people in Tehran, Isfahan, Shiraz, Mashhad, Yazd, Kermanshah, and Ardabil had reported hours-long outages, often without notice, in messages sent to Iran International on Sunday, and that the disruptions had also affected water supplies and internet access. The report said Mohammad Allahdad, chief executive of state electricity company Tavanir, announced Saturday that residential and commercial power restrictions would begin November 22 because of fuel shortages at power plants, and that outages could last two hours every other day, increasing to two hours daily if temperatures fall further. RFE/RL, in a report dated midnight CET Sunday, Nov 22 (5:00 p.m. CT Saturday), said the cuts started Nov 22 and quoted Allahdad telling state television that the outages are expected to last up to two hours a day depending on location. Nour News, in a report dated 8:09 a.m. Iran time Sunday, Nov 22, or 1 Azar 1405 (10:39 p.m. CT Saturday), and Eghtesad Online, in a report dated 8:29 a.m. Iran time Sunday (10:59 p.m. CT Saturday) that cited Nour News, said planned electricity restrictions began today and, citing the Tavanir chief executive, that the new restrictions may take the form of a two-hour outage over two days, or a maximum of two hours each day, that the timing is not fixed and may change with network conditions, and that customers would be informed through the Bargh-e Man system and app, the Bale messenger app, and text messages. Tavanir had announced on Saturday, Nov 21, that planned electricity restrictions on households and businesses would begin on Sunday, Nov 22, because fuel shortages were disrupting power generation, according to Iran International in a report dated 5:11 p.m. GMT Saturday, Nov 21 (11:11 a.m. CT), and to RFE/RL. Anar News, in a report updated at 12:05 a.m. UTC Sunday, Nov 22 (6:05 p.m. CT Saturday), citing BBC Persian, also said planned power outages began in Iran on Sunday, Nov 22, because of fuel shortages at power plants. No official customer count was given in those reports. No official nationwide remaining-customer count was found as of 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (9:30 p.m. Iran time Monday).

outages.updated: Nov 23, 2026, The National dated November 23, 2026, and marked updated at 5:00 AM, on scheduled cuts beginning and quoting Tavanir CEO Mohammad Allahdad on restrictions of up to two hours every other day or two hours daily if temperatures fall, and quoting President Masoud Pezeshkian via Isna on expected winter difficulties; Iran International dated 1:17 p.m. GMT Sunday, Nov 22 (= 7:17 a.m. CT), on scheduled cuts resuming and on Sunday reports from Tehran, Isfahan, Shiraz, Mashhad, Yazd, Kermanshah, and Ardabil of hours-long outages, often without notice, and quoting Allahdad on restrictions beginning Nov 22 because of fuel shortages; RFE/RL dated midnight CET Sunday, Nov 22 (= 5:00 p.m. CT Saturday); Nour News 8:09 a.m. Iran time Sunday (= 10:39 p.m. CT Saturday) and Eghtesad Online 8:29 a.m. Iran time Sunday (= 10:59 p.m. CT Saturday); earlier Tavanir Saturday announcement via Iran International 5:11 p.m. GMT Saturday (= 11:11 a.m. CT) and RFE/RL; Anar News updated 12:05 a.m. UTC Sunday (= 6:05 p.m. CT Saturday), citing BBC Persian; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23 (9:30 p.m. Iran time Monday), no official nationwide customer count found

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Drop Site News, in a Nov 20, 2026 report from Khartoum, said a particularly intense wave of drone strikes at the end of October and into November targeting power stations, fuel supplies, and electricity infrastructure had brought the country's power grid to the brink of collapse, and that two weeks after the wave of attacks, major substations remained out of service. Shaker Ismail, an engineer with the Sudanese Electricity Company, told Drop Site that repairing some of the country's most important power facilities could take months or longer, that high-capacity transformers and digital control systems had been damaged, and that replacement transformers must be manufactured to order abroad. Ismail said the Um Dabakir thermal power plant in White Nile State was badly damaged in an Oct 29 strike and forced to shut down, and that the Al-Markhiyat substation west of Omdurman was put out of service after an Oct 27 strike; he said affected areas continued to experience prolonged outages and scheduled power cuts as of this week. The report said the Sudan Electricity Holding Company and Ministry of Energy had yet to publicly announce the restoration of the major facilities damaged in the attacks. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. An earlier Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature said there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day, and, citing The Associated Press, said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. Al-Ghad Al-Sudani, in a report last updated Nov 22, 2026, said explosions and drone flights returned to Khartoum on Sunday morning, Nov 22, amid reports of attacks on military sites in various parts of the capital, and that the attacks coincided with power outages in large parts of the city; the report did not give a customer count or independently establish the cause of that outage. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found as of 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23.
outages.updated: Nov 20, 2026, Drop Site News report from Khartoum, quoting Sudanese Electricity Company engineer Shaker Ismail on major substations remaining out of service and on repairs that could take months; Nov 17, 2026 UN in Sudan / OHCHR report; Al Jazeera feature, published Nov 15; generation figure attributed to The Associated Press; Al-Ghad Al-Sudani last updated Nov 22, 2026, on Sunday morning drone attacks in Khartoum coinciding with power outages in large parts of the city, without a customer count or an independently established cause of that outage; rechecked 12:00 PM CT Monday, Nov 23, no official national customer count or official restoration timetable found
